Senet uses 4 d2 sticks to move
The game is over 5000 years old and uses only d2s for movement of pawns.

They look a bit different, but function similarly.

Most sticks used have a curvature on one end that actually tends to stack it a bit in favor of one side over the other.

They form "one die". If all four come up as nothing, it counts as five.

http://www.mastersgames.com/rules/senet-rules.htm

on a roll of two or three, no extra throw.

Although in this version, it counts as a 6: http://www.cs.brandeis.edu/~storer/JimPuzzles/GAMES/Senet/Senet.pdf

This is one way of playing, but seeing as the rules have been partially lost the style of play depends on which historian's version of the game you are playing.

The original rules aren't intact so different historians have placed different values, some use the 7 pawns per player and 5 instead of six on a blank roll while others use 5 pawns per player and six on a blank.
